title: v1/chat.completions: role_hint + stop_priority + normalized-logprobs envelope
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Adds OpenAI v1/chat.completions compatibility features: role_hint mapping to internal role aliases, stop_priority param to disambiguate multi-sentinel termination, and a stable logprobs envelope (partial_token_score -> token_logprobs). Streaming emits a compact 'token_delta' envelope to improve resilience. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in via compatibility flags.
description: Motivation: Some customers rely on nuanced OpenAI semantics around role/assistant attribution and stop sequence precedence; others expect a consistent logprobs envelope across streaming and non-streaming responses. This PR implements three small, well-scoped compatibility features for /v1/chat.completions: 1) role_hint - lightweight API-level mapping to preserve incoming role aliases (e.g., 'system_prompt' -> 'system') and to avoid downstream role-flipping during tool handoff; 2) stop_priority - an explicit integer precedence when multiple stop sequences intersect so clients can control which sentinel wins (helps in cases where both model-driven and app-driven stops coexist); 3) normalized logprobs envelope - replaces ad-hoc partial_token_score fields with a consistent token_logprobs array and per-chunk finalization metadata, so SDKs can rely on the same schema whether they receive streaming deltas or the final completion. Design: - role_hint is parsed at the adapter layer and produces a stable role mapping table attached to the request context; it does not mutate model weights or behavior except to label assistant/tool responses consistently in the chat transcript. - stop_priority is treated as an ordered array of tuples (sequence, priority); runtime short-circuits generation when the highest-priority sentinel matches. We provide a deterministic tie-breaker (longest-match then defined priority). - logprobs envelope: streaming now emits token_delta envelopes with {text, token_logprobs, cumulative_index, is_final_chunk} and the non-streaming path writes the same structure into choices[0].logprobs to make parity simple for SDKs. Rollout plan: feature gated behind compatibility flag openai_compat=v2; defaulting to off for now. We'll flip the flag for internal beta customers and monitor for regressions. Tests and validation: unit + integration tests added under tests/compat/, e2e with python/ts SDK snippets, and a small canary in prod routing 1% traffic to the new adapter. Backwards compatibility and docs: when flag is off, behavior is unchanged. Detailed migration notes added in docs/openapi/openai_v1_changelog.md. Risks: minor change surface on streaming envelope parsing; SDKs relying on ad-hoc fields must migrate. Ergo, staged rollout + telemetry on parsing errors. Summary of changes, tests, and next steps below.

review_comments: Luis Moreno: Nice decomposition — can you clarify whether role_hint can map multiple incoming aliases to a single canonical role? Eg 'assistant_bot' + 'assistant' -> 'assistant' ?
Anika Shah: Yes — role_hint accepts a mapping object. The adapter normalizes aliases into a canonical role name in the request context. Added unit tests for alias lists.
Chen Wu: stop_priority behaviour looks good but I'm worried about performance when many short stop sequences are registered. Did you add optimizations?

Anika Shah: We added a radix-tree based matcher inside stop_manager that avoids O(n*m) checks for high counts; performance microbench included under runtime/generation/benchmarks/stop_matcher.md. Also the majority of customers only provide a handful of stop sequences.
Marta Ruiz: breaking change risk for streaming SDKs — recommend we add a feature-detection field in the handshake so SDKs can switch parsers automatically.
Anika Shah: Agreed. Added 'compat_level' to the stream preface and updated SDK snippets in both python and typescript to auto-detect and parse token_delta envelopes. See sdk changes.
CI: Lint passed, unit tests initial run had two failures in test_logprobs_envelope.py due to ordering — fixed in c3e9b12 commit and re-ran. All checks green.
Release lead (Marta): marking this as release-blocker for 2026-02 minor as long as compat flag gating remains. Approved merge after resolving SDK handshake change.
